subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: ArithmeticBinder.BindAdd lines 29-41 and ArithmeticEmitter.EmitGiving (48-65). MATCHED: 'the initial evaluation consists of determining the sum of the operands PRECEDING the word GIVING' -- when `arithmeticGivingPhrase` is present the TO operand is folded into `addends` (`addends.AddRange(StatementBinder.DataRefs(toAddend).Select(host.Expr.BindExpr))`, line 33-34, with the in-code note that it used to be DROPPED), and only the GIVING operands become receivers (`givingRecv = host.Expr.Receivers(giving.receivingArithmeticOperand())`). 'This value is stored as the new value of EACH data item referenced by identifier-3' -- EmitGiving computes one value for the receiver SET and, with more than one receiver, Snapshots it before the per-receiver store loop, so all identifier-3s get the same value (Sec.14.7.7 GR4/NOTE 3). Value evidence, all spec-derived: ca4_giving_composite `ADD A B GIVING C` -> 1+2 = 3 (also proving the optional-word TO may be omitted); pb45 `ADD FUNCTION SQRT(W-Z) TO W-Q GIVING W-R` -> `ADD-GIVING=0011` = 2+9, which is precisely the 'operand-2 preceding GIVING is an ADDEND' half; pb66_float_edited_picture `ADD 1 0.5 GIVING E4` -> `ADD [ 15.000E-01]`. UNVERIFIED / BROKEN HALVES: (a) the rule's own words 'the value of operand-2 is the value of either LITERAL-2 or the data item referenced by identifier-2' cannot be exercised at all -- a literal-2 is unparseable (see FMT-14.9.2.2 defect 1), so the literal arm of GR2 has no implementation; (b) the second paragraph's standard-decimal / standard-binary equivalence is in the same state as GR-14.9.2.4-1 (STANDARD-BINARY rejected at DataBinder.cs:318; STANDARD-DECIMAL code-shared through NumericRenderer.CombineCore but with no ADD golden). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the grammar fix plus a golden `ADD 1 TO 2 GIVING C` -> 3, and a STANDARD-DECIMAL ADD ... GIVING golden. || UPHELD. Independently verified the operand ORDER the second paragraph fixes: GR2's expression is `(operand-11 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)`, operand-2 LAST, and BindAdd appends the TO operand to `addends` AFTER the operand list (line 33-34 runs on a list already built at line 26), so the fold order matches the printed expression -- which only matters under STANDARD-DECIMAL/float, i.e. exactly the unverified half. Also verified the operand-2 screen is not bypassed: `host.Expr.BindExpr` is `BindExprCore(node, OperandContext.Arithmetic)` (ExpressionBinder.cs:584), so the Sec.8.8.1.1 sending screen does apply to the harvested TO operand. I confirmed the pb66 line by grep: pb66_float_edited_picture.cob:83 `ADD 1 0.5 GIVING E4` with .out `ADD      [ 15.000E-01]`. || REFUTED (unverified half (a) is wider than stated): operand-2's identifier arm is also incomplete, not only its literal arm -- ISO 8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 makes a function-identifier an identifier, so `ADD 1 TO FUNCTION MAX(A B) GIVING C` is a legal spelling of operand-2 and is a parse error (see FMT-14.9.2.2). GR2's operand-2 is therefore unimplemented for TWO of the three shapes the standard admits there, not one. PB228 (2026-10-16), SECOND PARAGRAPH NOW PINNED: 2014/pb228_add_standard_decimal's GIV-1/GIV-2 (ADD X Z Y GIVING = 0.0000, ADD X Y Z GIVING = 0.0004) pin 'in the order in which they are specified', and GIV-3 (ADD X Z TO Y GIVING G3 = 0.0000) pins operand-2 LAST in (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2): taking the TO operand first, (Y + X) + Z, would give 0.0004. That is the order BindAdd's append of the TO operand after the operand list produces, previously protected by nothing because native addition is exact and commutative.
